 2 Food Recalls You Need To Know About This Week
 Megan Griffo 2026년 11월 7일 토 오전 11:31 UTC 0 Credit: Simply Recipes / Getty Images This week’s recalls include a ground cinnamon that was pulled due to potential lead contamination and a popular toddler snack recalled for posing a choking hazard. Check the product details below, and do not eat or serve any recalled products. This article provides an overview; for more information, refer to the notices linked below.
 Credit: Simply Recipes / Wise Wife Ground Cinnamon Recalled in 14 States Over Potential Lead Contamination
 On October 29, SLR Food Distribution Inc. announced a recall of Wise Wife Brand Ground Cinnamon. This came after testing by the Connecticut Agricultural Experiment Station found elevated lead levels. No illnesses have been reported to date.
 The company says short-term exposure to very low levels of lead may not cause symptoms. Children exposed over weeks to months, however, could experience permanent nervous system damage , including learning disorders and developmental defects.
 Product Information
 Product: Wise Wife Ground Cinnamon, 3.88 ounces, in a clear plastic container with a black screw-top cap
 UPC : 0688474302754 (printed on the back)
 Best-before date: April 25, 2027
 The cinnamon was sold at retail and grocery stores in Connecticut, Indiana, Kansas, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Nebraska, New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Texas, Virginia, and Wisconsin between September 8, 2025, and June 28, 2026.
 Advertisement
 If you have a container that matches the details above, do not use it. Discard it, or return it to the store where you bought it for a refund. Questions can go to the company at 516-437-3782, Monday through Friday from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. ET, or slrusaorder@gmail.com .
 Credit: Simply Recipes / Once Upon a Farm Once Upon a Farm Snacks Recalled Nationwide Over Choking Hazard
 Once Upon a Farm is recalling all lots and flavors of its Tractor Wheels Organic Toddler Soft-Baked Bars because they pose a choking hazard for toddlers ages 1 1/2 to 2 1/2. The company announced the recall on October 30, and the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) posted the notice on November 2.
 The FDA says it has received several reports of toddlers “suffering complete airway obstruction” after eating the bars, some requiring emergency response and hospital observation. Once Upon a Farm says the recall was based on three consumer complaints of choking.
 Product Information
 Product: Tractor Wheels Organic Toddler Soft-Baked Bars, all flavors and sizes
 Lot codes: All lots are included
 Best-by dates: October 30, 2026, to August 26, 2027, and expired products
 UPCs : See our full recall report for specific UPCs
 The bars were sold nationwide, including in Puerto Rico, online, and in stores. The FDA says that includes Costco, Target, and Walmart, and may include Amazon and other third-party sellers. Do not open or serve the bars. Throw them away, or return them to the store where you bought them for a refund. Questions can go to Once Upon a Farm at 888-983-1606, Monday through Friday from 6 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. PT and Saturday from 8 to 11 a.m. PT, or care@uponafarm.com .
